content:
incident-bot: Pager: Latency surge detected on edge-mux routing path in us-west1. p95 > 2s, p99 > 7s over last 8m, streaming stall rate +14%. Auto-severity: SEV2. Triggering on-call paging and live bridge.

oncall-mike: I'm on call. Joining bridge. Observing a big tail spike coincident with router policy churn. Creating thread for coordination.

raj (sre): Joining — I'm seeing a correlated increase in request fanout and a sharp rise in tail when requests hit lb-group-17. Heatmap shows one shard receiving 3x expected weight.

sophia (runtime): Confirmed. At 08:11 UTC we deployed route-affinity tweak (prefer-local buckets) to reduce cross-zone latency; rollout set weight adjustment to 1.2. Metrics show an accidental amplification on hot keys due to our shard weighting math.

natalie (eng-ml): Quick note: streaming clients rely on long-lived connections; increased fanout -> more streaming kv cache misses -> stalls. p50 okay but p99 exploding.

ben (support): Two enterprise customers reported partial streaming responses and reconnect loops. Ticket IDs: T-98712, T-98715. They've been escalated. Customer-impact flag set.

carol (product): Please tag impacted customers as "NA-enterprise" and prepare a brief post-incident note if this becomes a SEV1. We need estimated time to mitigate.

oncall-mike: Action plan proposal: 1) Roll back the route-affinity tweak (quick rollback). 2) Temporarily add a routing override to divert traffic away from lb-group-17. 3) Flush KV prefix cache on affected routers. 4) Monitor p95/p99 and customer reports. Approve rollback?

raj (sre): Approve rollback. I can push a rollback to the routing config. I'll also add a short-term weight cap to prevent hot amplification.

sophia (runtime): I'll prepare the cache flush playbook and watch for elevated CPU on routers after rollback (we saw brief CPU bumps in canary).

deploy-bot: Rollout detected: route-affinity-v2 -> started rollback by raj (sre) at 08:22:41 UTC. Target: us-west1-edge-mux.

raj (sre): Rolling back now. Command: ```/deploy rollback route-affinity-v2 --env=us-west1 --reason="hot amplification causing tail"```

deploy-bot: Rollback completed successfully at 08:23:05 UTC. No failed hosts.

oncall-mike: Now applying routing override to steer traffic off lb-group-17: ```/router update-weight --group=lb-group-17 --weight=0.2 --scope=temporary --ttl=10m```

raj (sre): Override applied. Checking heatmap... shard weight for lb-group-17 dropped from 3.1x -> 0.21x. Good.

sophia (runtime): Initiating KV prefix flush on edge mux nodes in us-west1: ```kubectl exec -n runtime edge-mux-*-usw1 -- /usr/local/bin/kv-cache-flush --prefix=streaming:kv:```. Rolling through 4 pods with 30s stagger to avoid mass reconnects.

ben (support): Noted. I messaged the two customers with interim update: "We are rolling back a recent routing change and diverting traffic. Expect improved streaming stability within minutes. Will follow up with root cause and timeline."

natalie (eng-ml): From metrics: p95 dropped from ~2.2s to ~0.9s within 3m of rollback. p99 trending down but still elevated at ~2.8s. Streaming stall rate down to +3% (was +14%).

carol (product): Good. Any sign of global spillover / region skew?

raj (sre): We're seeing residual effects in egress affinity tables; east regions had a small bump due to cross-zone fallback but within SLO. I'll run a quick diff on routing tables to ensure no seed drift: ```git diff routeset/us-west1@HEAD~1..HEAD```

raj (sre): Diff shows the prefer-local weight multiplier was accidentally applied multiplicatively with hotkey weights in the combined policy, producing >1 amplification. I've opened PR #4512 to fix the combine logic to clamp at 1.0.

oncall-mike: Is there any need for a hotfix to rollback clients or models?

natalie (eng-ml): No client-side changes required. This is server routing/weight math only. No model degradation observed.

sophia (runtime): Monitoring host metrics — cpu and mem stable. Connection churn spiked briefly during cache flush but within thresholds.

deploy-bot: Canary telemetry: stream-start-success rate back to baseline in us-west1 canaries at 08:28 UTC.

ben (support): Customers acknowledged the message; one says they're seeing improved session starts. I'll keep them updated and mark as "monitoring".

oncall-mike: Current status: rollback completed, temporary override applied, cache flush in progress, p95 improving, p99 reducing but not fully recovered. Continue monitoring for 30m.

raj (sre): Next steps: 1) Merge fix to the routing combine logic (PR #4512). 2) Add a unit test to prevent multiplicative stacking. 3) Plan a staged re-rollout with weight cap safety. 4) Run a short chaos test to verify no hot amplification on canary.

carol (product): Keep comms ready. If p99 falls below 1.5s and no new customer complaints in 30m, we can de-escalate.

natalie (eng-ml): I'll add a temporary evaluation check to Redwood Optimize to alert if combination of features yields >1.1 amplification on any shard.

sophia (runtime): Also recommending we add a telemetry tag when route-affinity toggles are active so incident-bot can surface config-change-correlated alerts automatically.

oncall-mike: Thanks all. I'll keep bridge open and post updates. If condition stabilizes by 09:00 UTC, we'll close.

incident-bot: Update: metrics snapshot at 08:34 UTC — p95=0.92s, p99=1.9s, streaming stall delta +2.8%.

raj (sre): PV: I've deployed PR #4512 to staging with unit tests. Will aim for canary in 2 hours after we validate no regression.

ben (support): Customers T-98712/T-98715 set to "monitoring"; outreach message logged.

carol (product): Preparing a short incident note draft for customers in case follow-up required.

natalie (eng-ml): Logged evaluation rule: "route-weight-combine-clamp" with severity warning.

oncall-mike: Closing loop for now — leaving notes in the incident tracker and will call for postmortem if root cause requires cross-team follow-up.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Auto tags: routing, live-rollback, hot-amplification.

oncall-mike: Thanks folks. If anything new pops up ping this thread and I will re-open bridge.

ben (support): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
